decisions.reason: As a large firm with portfolio slack and global agricultural customers, it is likely to keep this niche crate unless its export-oriented demand persistently falls below aspirations.
Its continued stand-alone presentation through 2019 suggests comparatively strong acceptance, so behavioral theory implies little pressure to reallocate resources away from it.
A stackable plastic crate fits the firm’s core reusable-packaging range, and in a large German manufacturer such close-to-core products are usually retained unless results clearly disappoint.

This pallet is adjacent to the established pallet business and therefore likely benefits from existing capabilities and customer relationships, reducing the chance of withdrawal despite uncertain standout performance.

The move from a dedicated page to only a mention hints at weaker-than-hoped traction, but the firm’s size and product breadth make continued retention for another year still somewhat more likely than discontinuation.

Although its reduced website prominence may signal performance below aspiration, it remains close to the core pallet line and can be carried longer in a large firm with engineering and manufacturing slack.
